source.name: WMO State of Global Water Resources 2024 and UN World Water Development Report 2025

cadence: Annual WMO water-resource report and UN World Water Development Report release review.
provenance: Official WMO 2024 global glacier mass-balance assessment paired with the official UN glacier-preservation and UNESCO/UN-Water human-dependence assessment. Glacier mass loss and glacier-plus-snow dependence are retained as separate fields.
uncertainty: The WMO global mass estimate combines about 500 field-monitored glaciers and geodetic measurements covering more than 200,000 glaciers. Preliminary 2024 observations, regional scaling and mass-balance methods affect the estimate. The human figure covers melt from glaciers and snow and must not be interpreted as glacier-only volume share or observed shortage.
failure_behavior: Retain the last reviewed assessment pair and mark stale; reject changed glacier-region denominators, missing mass units or an unreconciled dependence definition. Never relabel glacier-plus-snow dependence as glacier-only supply, convert exposure to realized shortage, or add coastal sea-level exposure.

assessment.small_glacier_region_peak_water_status: most have likely passed peak water
source_locators: WMO State of Global Water Resources 2024, Snow cover and glaciers chapter: 450 Gt lost, all 19 regions, third consecutive year.
WMO report methods: approximately 500 field glaciers and more than 200,000 geodetically measured glaciers, covering 96 percent of global glaciers.
UN International Year of Glaciers Preservation key message 7: more than 2 billion people rely on melt from glaciers and snow for freshwater.

excluded_from_scoring: coastal population exposed to sea-level rise
mountain-water users not explicitly tied to glacier or snow melt
